full_caption: Foxglove Landing Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellant, v. Marbury Hollow Property Group, Inc., Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Foxglove Landing Capital Servicing, LLC, as servicer for the holder of the note, commenced this foreclosure against Marbury Hollow Property Group, Inc. with respect to the property at 264 Mill Race Way, Harrowgate, AR, securing an original principal balance of $295,000.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The statute of limitations on a foreclosure action runs from acceleration, not from the original maturity date. Where an earlier acceleration was withdrawn by dismissal of a prior action, the limitations clock is reset as to installments coming due thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Marbury Hollow Property Group, Inc. made 8 payments under a trial loan-modification plan and was thereafter denied a permanent modification on the ground of an unverified escrow shortfall of $1,450.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: A servicer that accepts payments under a trial plan and then denies permanent modification without the review the plan promises may be estopped from asserting the default those payments were tendered to cure.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The equity of redemption may be exercised at any time before the sale is confirmed. Tender must be of the full accelerated balance plus costs, not merely of the arrearage, once acceleration has validly occurred.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Post-sale, the purchaser takes subject to any bona fide tenancy of record. A tenant in possession under a lease predating the mortgage is not divested by the sale.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A deficiency judgment is available only where the foreclosure sale price is confirmed as commercially reasonable. The bid of $390,000 against an appraised value of $475,000 is presumptively unreasonable and requires an evidentiary hearing.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The allonge produced at trial was undated and was not physically affixed to the note when the original was tendered for inspection. An allonge must be affixed to the instrument to be effective as an endorsement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The mortgage requires that a notice of default be sent to the borrower's last known address, specifying the default, the action required to cure, a date not less than 15 days from the notice by which the default must be cured, and the borrower's right to reinstate.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Standing to foreclose requires that the plaintiff hold the note, endorsed in blank or to the plaintiff, at the time the complaint is filed. A later-acquired endorsement does not cure a standing defect existing at filing.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Strict compliance with contractual notice conditions is a condition precedent to acceleration. The notice sent to Marbury Hollow Property Group, Inc. omitted the reinstatement advisory and was therefore ineffective to accelerate the debt.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: The judgment of foreclosure is vacated and the cause remanded with directions to dismiss without prejudice for failure to satisfy the notice condition precedent.

sections.heading: RIDER D — SALE, DEFICIENCY AND SURPLUS
sections.text: Any sale shall be conducted publicly after publication for 4 consecutive weeks. No deficiency judgment shall be entered unless the court finds, after an evidentiary hearing, that the sale price was commercially reasonable in relation to the fair market value of the Property. Any surplus remaining after satisfaction of the debt, costs and junior liens of record shall be paid to Borrower within 30 days of confirmation.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Successors, Assigns and Runs With the Land
sections.text: The benefits and burdens created by this instrument touch and concern the subject land, are intended by the parties to run with the land in perpetuity, and bind every successor in title with notice, actual, constructive or inquiry. A conveyance of the benefited parcel carries the benefit whether or not this instrument is mentioned in the deed of conveyance.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Ardenne.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Interpretation and Construction Against Drafter
sections.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect construction. The singular includes the plural. This instrument is the product of negotiation between the parties, and no rule of construction requiring interpretation against the drafting party shall apply. Restrictions on the use of land shall nonetheless be construed in favor of the free use of the land.
